entries.content: Using `caveman` because requested: terse updates, full technical detail. First read skill and feature header; then read every referenced file except header `agents`; then inspect code before design edit.

---
name: caveman
description: >
  Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts output tokens 65% (measured) by speaking like caveman
  while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra,
  wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra.
  Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens",
  "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
---

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked â€” quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) â€” tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (â†’) either â€” own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese â†’ reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish â†’ reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim â€” unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only â€” never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |
| **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X â†’ Y) â€” measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully æ–‡è¨€æ–‡. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (ä¹‹/ä¹ƒ/ç‚º/å…¶) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example â€” "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "çµ„ä»¶é »é‡ç¹ªï¼Œä»¥æ¯ç¹ªæ–°ç”Ÿå°è±¡åƒç…§æ•…ã€‚ä»¥ useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹ã€‚"
- wenyan-full: "æ¯ç¹ªæ–°ç”Ÿå°è±¡åƒç…§ï¼Œæ•…é‡ç¹ªï¼›ä»¥ useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹å‰‡å…ã€‚"
- wenyan-ultra: "æ–°åƒç…§å‰‡é‡ç¹ªã€‚useMemo åŒ…ä¹‹ã€‚"

Example â€” "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No per-request handshake."
- wenyan-full: "æ± è“„å·²é–‹ä¹‹é€£ï¼Œä¸é€è«‹è€Œæ–°é–‹ï¼Œçœæ¡æ‰‹ä¹‹è²»ã€‚"
- wenyan-ultra: "æ± è“„é€£ï¼Œå…é€è«‹æ–°é–‹ï¼Œçœæ¡æ‰‹ã€‚"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` â€” order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example â€” destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.
- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.
- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.
- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.
- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).
- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.
- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.

---

## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)

- **Buttons:** `Button variant="contained"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant="outlined"` = secondary; `variant="text"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).
- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.
- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.
- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.
- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.
- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.
- **Select:** `size="small"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.
- **Menu / context menu:** all `Menu` / `MenuItem` dropdowns and right-click context menus are dense by default through the theme. Call sites must not set density; `Select` option lists inherit the same density.
- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.
- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop â€” except that a dialog holding unsaved multi-field input may refuse `backdropClick` (return early from `onClose(event, reason)`) so a stray click on the scrim cannot discard typed values; `Esc` and the Cancel button must still close it, and Cancel stays visible and enabled, including while loading.
- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No "click to add" placeholder blocks.

---

## 9. Definition of done for a new component

1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.
2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.
3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.
4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.
5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.
6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).

Component-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.

* make columns resizable
* instead of buttons, use a link to open a child object or list. don't use 'open fieldname' but keep it shorter 'open'

## Current state

`JsonArrayEditor` renders arrays through a virtualized MUI table. Object-only arrays use the first-seen union of object field names as data columns; primitive, mixed, and empty arrays use one `values` column. Column widths come from browser table layout and cannot be changed by the user.

Nested object and array cells render outlined buttons whose visible label includes the field name, such as `Open details`. These controls drill into the value through `JsonDataDocument`; they do not navigate to a URL.

## implementation details

* Make every data column resizable from its header. Keep the selection-checkbox column fixed. Use explicit column widths for header and virtualized body cells so both remain aligned, and allow horizontal scrolling when the combined widths exceed the editor width.
* Store array column widths as view data in `JsonDataDocument`, keyed by JSON location and column name. `JsonArrayEditor` reads widths from the document snapshot and calls focused document methods during resize; React components do not become another state owner.
* Add a keyboard-focusable separator to each resizable header boundary. Pointer drag uses pointer movement from the width captured on pointer down, then clamps to a named minimum width. `ArrowLeft` and `ArrowRight` resize by a named step; `Home` selects the minimum. Pointer cancellation and lost capture end resizing.
* Keep the separator hit target wide enough for pointer and touch input, but draw a centered one-pixel line. Use theme `divider` color at rest and `primary.main` for hover, focus, and active drag states.
* Replace each nested-value outlined button with a link-styled button. Visible text is only `Open`; an accessible name includes the field or value column and one-based row number. Keep `JsonDataDocument.drillInto` behavior, keyboard activation, and breadcrumb navigation unchanged.
* Extend `json_data_editor.test.tsx` with pointer and keyboard resizing, minimum-width clamping, header/body width alignment, horizontal overflow, short visible link text, contextual accessible names, and nested object and array drill-in coverage. Verify separator and link styling in light and dark themes manually because these are visual requirements.

## acceptance criteria

* Each JSON array data column has a header separator that resizes that column by pointer or keyboard; the selection column remains fixed.
* Starting a pointer drag does not change column width until the pointer moves. Width changes by pointer movement distance and never becomes narrower than the defined minimum.
* Resized header and virtualized body cells stay aligned. When total column width exceeds available space, the table scrolls horizontally without shrinking columns below their minimum.
* Header separators expose separator role, vertical orientation, current width, and minimum width. Hover, keyboard focus, and active drag states remain visible in light and dark themes.
* Nested object and array cells show link-styled `Open` controls. Each control's accessible name identifies its column and row, and pointer or keyboard activation opens the correct child value.
* Existing inline scalar editing, row virtualization, selection, add, delete, copy, cut, paste, breadcrumbs, and read-only behavior remain unchanged.
* Focused JSON editor tests and `npm run lint` pass.

+
+## Current state
+
+`PrimaryChangesDialog` opens when worktree integration finds changes in the primary project branch. `PrimaryChangesService.confirm` marks the service busy, calls `StorageService.commitPrimaryChanges`, and closes the dialog after success. `WorktreeService` then retries integration. A failed commit is reported through `dialogService`; the dialog remains open with the entered message so the user can retry.
+
+The shared busy state covers both committing and moving a file to trash. It disables the OK and trash controls and makes Cancel a no-op, but it does not identify which operation is running. During a commit, the dialog shows no progress animation or status text, and the commit-message field remains editable. The merge-conflict dialog already uses the intended pattern: an informational alert with `CircularProgress`, explanatory text, and a progress state on the primary action.
+
+## implementation details
+
+* Add commit-specific state to `PrimaryChangesService`, separate from its generic busy state. Expose that state through a granular `EventTarget` event and a `useSyncExternalStore` hook. File-trash operations must remain busy without being presented as commits.
+* Set commit-specific state immediately before `commitPrimaryChanges` starts. Clear it after failure, and reset it when the review finishes after success, cancellation, service reinitialization, or cleanup.
+* While commit-specific state is active, show an informational alert in `PrimaryChangesDialog` with an accessible `CircularProgress` and text stating that project changes are being committed. Change the OK button label to `Committing...` and include a small spinner, matching the merge-conflict completion feedback.
+* Disable the commit-message field, OK, Cancel, file-trash actions, backdrop close, and Escape close until the commit finishes. The commit is non-cancellable: after the storage call starts, dialog controls cannot stop it safely.
+* Keep the dialog open while the commit promise is pending. On success, preserve current behavior: close the review, resolve it as confirmed, then let `WorktreeService` retry integration. On failure, remove progress feedback, keep the message and file list, report the existing error, and restore controls for retry.
+* Add focused component tests with a deferred commit promise to verify immediate feedback, accessible progress, disabled controls, pending-dialog visibility, success closure, and failure recovery. Add service tests for commit-specific state and events. Keep storage and worktree integration contracts unchanged.
+
+## acceptance criteria
+
+* Starting a commit immediately shows a progress animation and text that identifies project changes as the operation in progress.
+* While the commit is pending, the dialog stays open and no field, file action, button, backdrop click, or Escape key can start another action or close the review.
+* Moving a file to trash does not show commit progress or the `Committing...` label.
+* Successful commit closes the dialog, resolves the review as confirmed, and allows the existing integration retry to continue.
+* Failed commit removes progress feedback, preserves the commit message and file list, reports the existing error, and permits retry or cancellation.
+* Progress feedback is accessible and uses theme-backed MUI styling consistent with merge-conflict completion feedback.
+* Focused `PrimaryChangesService` and `PrimaryChangesDialog` tests pass, and `npm run lint` passes.

I read the spec and the code and made three tasks. Here is the plan. Nothing is edited yet; I'm waiting for your approval.

## Change plan for J_74

**Block 1: commit state in the service** (`app/src/services/project/primary_changes_service.ts`, `app/src/components/hooks/use_primary_changes.ts`)
- Add a private `committing` flag, an `isCommitting()` getter, a `PRIMARY_CHANGES_COMMITTING_EVENT = 'committing'` event, and a private `setCommitting()` that fires the event only when the value changes.
- In `confirm()`, `setCommitting(true)` runs right before `commitPrimaryChanges`, and only when there are changes. An empty list skips the commit, so it shows no progress.
- If the commit fails, clear both the commit flag and the busy flag, then report the error as today.
- `finishReview()` clears the commit flag. That covers success, cancel, `init()` and `clear()`.
- `trash()` only sets busy, never the commit flag.
- Add a `usePrimaryChangesCommitting()` hook.
- New service tests:
  - the flag and its event are set while the commit is pending;
  - the flag is cleared after failure, with the message and list kept;
  - it is reset after success;
  - trash never sets it.

**Block 2: progress display in the dialog**
- **New `primary_changes_commit_progress.tsx`:** shows an `Alert severity="info"` with `CircularProgress aria-label="Committing project changes"` and the text "Committing project changes...", only while a commit runs. It looks the same as the merge-conflict "Finishing integration" alert.
- **New `primary_changes_cancel_button.tsx`:** Cancel is disabled while a commit runs. The dialog itself doesn't subscribe to the state, because the smallest component that shows a value should own that subscription.
- **`primary_changes_confirm_button.tsx`:** while committing, the label becomes `Committing...`, with a small `CircularProgress` (16px, `aria-hidden`) as the start icon.
- **`primary_change_message_field.tsx`:** the field is `disabled` while committing.
- **Trash buttons:** already disabled whenever the dialog is busy, so no change.
- **Backdrop click and Escape:** `onClose` calls `cancel()`, which already does nothing while busy. I'll add no extra flag and will test that this works.

**Block 3: tests, lint, status**
- New tests in `primary_changes_dialog.test.tsx`, using a commit promise the test resolves or rejects itself:
  - progress shows immediately;
  - the progressbar has an accessible name;
  - the field, OK, Cancel and trash are disabled;
  - Escape keeps the dialog open;
  - success closes it and resolves the review as true;
  - failure removes the progress, keeps the message and list, and enables the controls again;
  - trashing a file shows no commit progress.
- Run only the two related test files, then `npm run lint`.
- Set `status: ready` in `C:\Users\janbo\Documents\dev\md2\design\feature_descriptions\J_74_...md`.

One unclear point in the spec: the message field and Cancel will be disabled only during a commit, not during a trash, because the spec names only the commit. Say if you want them disabled during trash as well.

Approve?

entries.content:
J_74 is implemented. While a commit runs, the dialog now shows a spinner with "Committing project changes..." and every control is locked. The two related test files pass (22 tests), and `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` are clean. I did not run the full test suite.

**Service** (`app/src/services/project/primary_changes_service.ts`)
- A new commit flag sits next to the existing busy flag, which still covers both committing and moving a file to trash. Each change to the commit flag fires a new `'committing'` event.
- `confirm()` sets the flag right before the storage commit starts. It only does that when there are files to commit, because an empty list skips the commit.
- A failed commit clears the flag along with busy, so the user can retry.
- Ending the review clears it too, which covers success, cancel, `init()` and `clear()`.
- Moving a file to trash never sets it.

**Hook:** `usePrimaryChangesCommitting()` in `app/src/components/hooks/use_primary_changes.ts`.

**Dialog**
- New `primary_changes_commit_progress.tsx`: an info alert with a spinner labelled "Committing project changes", styled like the merge-conflict "Finishing integration" alert.
- New `primary_changes_cancel_button.tsx`: Cancel is disabled while the commit runs.
- `primary_changes_confirm_button.tsx`: while committing, the label reads `Committing...` with a small spinner.
- `primary_change_message_field.tsx`: the field is disabled while committing.
- Trash buttons, backdrop click and Escape needed no change. Trash buttons were already disabled while busy. Backdrop click and Escape call `cancel()`, which already does nothing while busy.

**Tests**
- Service: four new tests:
  - the flag and its event while the commit is pending, then after success;
  - the flag cleared after a failure, with the message and list kept;
  - the flag reset when the service is cleared mid-commit;
  - trash never setting the flag.
- Dialog: three new tests, using a commit or trash promise the test settles itself:
  - while committing: progress shows, the controls are disabled and Escape does not close the dialog; success then closes it and resolves the review as confirmed;
  - after a failure: the progress is removed, the message and list are kept, the error is reported and the controls work again;
  - a pending trash shows no commit progress.

The `status` field in `md2/design/feature_descriptions/J_74_uncommitted_project_changes_dialog_improvements.md` is now `ready`.
